newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: SE Asian Cocoa - Prices up on New York rally.
newsitem.headline: SE Asian Cocoa - Prices up on New York rally.

text.p: Cocoa prices soared in Malaysia and Indonesia on Wednesday, inspired by the overnight rise of New York cocoa futures to 2-1/2 year highs and on news of cocoa imports by Brazil, traders said.
"Prices are higher in line with gains in New York overnight," one cocoa trader in Indonesia said. "The news from Brazil is also keeping sentiment bullish."
One dealer in Indonesia said local cocoa prices were expected to maintain their upward momentum into next week on sustained buying interest.

"Prices are expected to increase next week because demand is good and the market is bullish," he said. "I expect London futures to open higher later today as it catches up with New York's sharp increase on Tuesday."
The Malaysian Cocoa Board quoted Standard Malaysian Cocoa (SMC) Grade 1A out of Tawau at an average of 3,387 ringgit a tonne, up 77 ringgit from last week.
The board quoted the SMC 1B grade out of Tawau at an average of 3,315 ringgit, up 57 ringgit from the previous week.
Traders offered the SMC 1A at 3,357 ringgit a tonne and the SMC IB at 3,390-3,400 ringgit.
In Indonesia, prices were quoted at 3,085-3,100 rupiah/kg in Ujung Pandang, capital of the key growing region of South Sulawesi, compared with 2,950-2,975 rupiah last week.
The rise was triggered by New York, where the most-active May futures contract in the CSCE shot up US$59 on the day to end at $1,512 a tonne, after ranging from $1,520 to $1,440 in intra-day trading.

It was highest level since July 1994 as speculators bought heavily due to bullish technical indicators, U.S. traders said. The rosy sentiment was aided by news that Brazil had given three companies the go-ahead to import 4,000 tonnes of Indonesian
cocoa beans to make up for a shortfall at the start of the Bahian midcrop.
One trader said the 4,000-tonne consignment was expected to leave Indonesia shortly.
"I heard that the beans are ready for shipment, which is expected to take place shortly," he said. "I heard the prices offered by the Brazilian companies were quite good."
But business in Malaysia remained slow with one cocoa trader saying local consumers, including confectioners and grinders, were still comfortably stocked on beans.
Supply could tighten though after April due to the traditionally poor first harvest of beans from the main growing of Tawau in the eastern state of Sabah.

"With prices surging, I think there will be some caution on the domestic front for a while," a dealer in Malaysia said. "But imports will have to start by end of April as there may be shortages then."
